nodes.label: In-App Update System
nodes.rationale: The app checks GitHub Releases for newer versions and prompts in-app to download and install the APK, with mandatory updates blocking use until updated — avoiding dependence on an app store update channel.

nodes.label: Row Level Security (RLS)
nodes.rationale: The publishable key is a client-side key used by the app while authorization must be enforced server-side via Supabase Authentication and RLS — client-side configuration must never be a substitute for server-side authorization.

nodes.label: Never-Commit Secrets Policy
nodes.rationale: Supabase service-role keys, Firebase service-account credentials, private signing keys, and production secrets must never enter the repo; the Supabase publishable key is a client-side key protected by authentication and RLS rather than secrecy.

nodes.label: Merge Hard-Delete Resurrection Limitation
nodes.rationale: Hard DELETE leaves no tombstone, so a merge from an older backup cannot tell 'never existed' from 'deleted since' and re-inserts deleted rows; a deleted_records tombstone table would close the gap — explicitly called out as out of scope rather than silently assumed away.

nodes.label: Merge Rule: Last-Write-Wins + Insert-If-Absent
nodes.rationale: Merge reuses the exact last-write-wins rule SyncRepositoryImpl already applies against Supabase rather than inventing a second conflict rule; append-only ledgers with no reliable timestamp get insert-if-absent only so existing rows are never overwritten.

nodes.label: Restore Resync via Existing Sync Pipeline
nodes.norm_label: restore resync via existing sync pipeline
nodes.rationale: Every restored row with isSynced=false is re-enqueued onto the existing sync_queue and SyncManager.scheduleImmediateSync is called once, so restore reuses the normal upsert-by-id path and can never create a duplicate Supabase row; restore never talks to Supabase directly.

nodes.label: Offline-First Architecture (Room/SQLCipher + Supabase Sync)
nodes.rationale: The clinic must keep operating without network: an encrypted local Room database is the working source of truth, with a sync queue and retry handling pushing changes to Supabase.

nodes.label: Responsible Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: Report vulnerabilities privately with no public GitHub issues and allow reasonable time before disclosure; security testing must not access other users' data, obtain unauthorized credentials, disrupt service, or use real patient information.

nodes.label: CI Firebase Configuration Stub
nodes.rationale: google-services.json is intentionally not committed; this temporary CI configuration allows the Google Services Gradle plugin to configure the debug build, and it is removed after the build steps.

nodes.label: CI Firebase Configuration Stub
nodes.rationale: google-services.json is intentionally excluded from Git; a temporary CI-only configuration lets the Google Services Gradle plugin configure the debug build, and it is removed with if:always() after the build.

nodes.label: Use Graphify Before Grep
nodes.rationale: This repository is indexed by the Graphify code graph; query definitions, callers, blast radius, and test coverage through Graphify MCP before reaching for grep or file reads, falling back only for literal strings or non-indexed files.

nodes.label: Ponytail Lazy Senior Dev Mode
nodes.rationale: The best code is the code never written: climb the ladder (YAGNI, reuse existing code, stdlib, native platform, installed deps, one line, then minimum code) only after fully understanding the problem; shortest working diff wins.

nodes.label: Root-Cause Bug Fixing
nodes.rationale: A bug report names a symptom: grep every caller of the touched function and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than a guard per caller, and patching only the reported path leaves sibling callers broken.

nodes.label: Backup Versioning / BackupMigrator
nodes.rationale: backupVersion is checked on read so a newer backup fails fast before anything is touched; because Json ignoreUnknownKeys plus field defaults are already used, most additive changes need no version bump, and BackupMigrator is the extension point for a future 1-to-2 mapping.

nodes.label: App Logo - Child with Protective Arc
nodes.norm_label: app logo - child with protective arc

nodes.label: Worker Supabase JWT Verification (HS256/JWKS)
nodes.rationale: SUPABASE_JWKS_URL is the preferred verification path for ES256/RS256 access tokens; HS256 via SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET remains supported for backward compatibility with legacy tokens.

nodes.label: Per-Account Backup Isolation
nodes.rationale: The account id is derived from the verified JWT sub claim and checked against the D1 row's stored account_id — never from anything the client supplied in the URL or body — which is what stops one clinic from reading another clinic's backup by changing an id.

nodes.label: Local SQLCipher Database Encryption
nodes.rationale: Local database at rest uses SQLCipher with a key from Android Keystore-backed EncryptedSharedPreferences — device-bound and never leaving the device, which is why it cannot be reused for portable backups.

nodes.label: Portable Backup Encryption (AES-256-GCM / PBKDF2)
nodes.rationale: Portable backups need password-based encryption independent of the device-bound database key because a backup must be restorable on a different device/install; the password is never stored for manual exports, and there is deliberately no server-side escrow — a lost password means the backup cannot be recovered.

nodes.label: Native R2 Binding (No Access Keys)
nodes.rationale: The Worker uses a native R2 binding instead of the S3-compatible API so no R2 access key or secret exists anywhere in the project — not in the Android app (the hard requirement) and not even as a Worker secret, since a binding needs none.
